abandon custom and go alone,
ascend to before the Great Beginning,
gaze upon the dawn of the limitless void,
let thought flow freely beyond all bounds,
let the will be vast and thus spread out,
drifting and soaring through the four courses of time,
circling and soaring in the eight directions.
To wish to proceed without restraint and indistinct,
to wash and float without limit, so that insignificant conduct cannot be faulted,
and sages and worthies are not worth praise.
To undergo transformation and shifting,
in harmony with the spirit.
To make boundlessness the dwelling place,
to use the cosmos as a home,
to strengthen the eight dimensions and dwell in peace,
to govern things and live forever:
if so, only then may one be said to be truly wealthy and noble.
Therefore, to not measure one’s virtue with that of Yáo and Shùn,
nor compare one’s deeds with Tāng and Wǔ;
kings and dukes are not worthy to be matched,
how could Yángqiū possibly match such unbridled scope,
even Heaven and Earth cannot surpass such longevity,
how could Guǎngchéngzǐ ever be regarded as one’s equal.
To stir the eight winds and raise one’s voice,
follow the lofty traces of Yuán Jí;
to don the nine heavens and travel far,
summon the clouds and ride the flying dragon,
command above and below, ruling all,
surpassing past and present with nothing the same;
what do fame and profit in the world amount to for such a one!
Therefore, to lift Qí and tread Chǔ,
to take Zhào and step on Qín,
in less than a morning, there is no one under Heaven,
east, west, south, north—none to be called a neighbor.
How sad!
Your adornments—
as I see it,
where will they find their place?"
At this, the master departed from the myriad entanglements,
traveling across wild paths and vast obscurity,
flowing and expanding in endless wanderings,
passing deep abysses,
striding across the blue heavens,
glancing back and calmly beholding all.
Thus does he roam at ease to prolong his years,
not persisting in fleeting unions,
dispersing and arriving below,
swiftly splitting and wandering apart,
drifting and gliding,
tempests driving, clouds floating,
attaining the Shaking Light,
dashing straight through the midst of the Great Beginning,

What is the Great Beginning like?
Without after or before,
none can reach its limit,

Ascend to its myriad heavens for a full view,

Roaming at ease and far from all boundaries,
traveling the Great Road without end.

to traverse Heaven and Earth by a straight path.

to roam the infinite wilderness to the left,
to the right, the unfathomable vastness,
upwards, to listen far and hear no sound,
downward, to gaze deeply and see no pattern,
to act without having and dwell among spirits,
to soar forever in the realm of Purity.

Focus essence and spirit, make intention calm,

The qúyù bird does not cross the Jì,
the Luò does not cross the Wèn,
men of the world,
are likewise.
Never venturing beyond their bounds,
let alone beyond the four seas,
or outside Heaven and Earth.
But as for the master,
he regards Heaven and Earth as no more than an egg.
For petty things and small men to debate the length or shortness thereof,
to judge right or wrong,
is that not truly a pity!
Letter on Grasping the Red Ape
"Letter on Grasping the Red Ape."
I never expected to dream suddenly of grasping a red ape,
its strength was greater than leopards and tigers,
after a long time wrestling, I reversed my position.
So I gazed at Heaven,
turned my back on the earth,
saw the furthest depths,
and was just about on target.
But since I do not understand,
how can I not worry.
Is it auspicious?
Hold me.
Is it inauspicious?
Tell me in detail.
Third month,
Ruǎn Jí, to Bái Yáojūn.

Ten Four-Character Poems by Ruǎn Jí
"Ten Four-Character Poems by Ruǎn Jí"
The solar essence blazes fiercely,
and plants and trees stand bleak and somber.
Valley winds fan the heat,
and dense clouds cover the sky in heavy gloom.
Flashing lightning streaks with radiance,
and thunder's roar leaves a lingering sound.
Drizzling rain descends and gathers,
drifting far over the northern woods.
The light boat glides on,
at times floating, at times sinking.
I grieve for the past and feel sorrow for what is to come,
cherishing the ancients and lamenting the present.
Life has its fate,
and the times bring deep anxieties.
Why express my thoughts,
but to whistle and sing in long chants?
Who can uphold steadfast resolve,
pure as jade, strong as gold?
Endure sorrow without being wounded,
abide in joy without falling into excess.
Respectfully accepting wise instruction,
I thereby console my heart.
Forms established shine forth and rotate,
and Yin and Yang proceed in their paths.
The autumn wind arrives early and severe,
and white dew falls through the night.
Tall woods wither and perish,
luxuriant grasses lose their glory.
The good season passes suddenly,
the morning sun leans to the west.
All things have a beginning and an end,
who can long sustain fullness?
The constellation Tàiwēi opens the way,
and the three celestial bodies lower their essence.
Lofty are the gathered dragons,
leaping and soaring in the purple court.
Their scales are scattered and spent,
while those of high rank ride on clear roads.
Some withdraw, some remain silent,
hiding their glow and concealing their forms.
I wish to preserve this day,
forever attuned to a long life.
The celestial mechanisms revolve swiftly,
and the four seasons are declared in due order.
Winter days are bleak and mournful,
dark clouds shroud the sky.
Pure ice spreads across the marshes,
and white snow clings to the mountains.
□□ passes away and departs,
like the moving current of a river.
Who among people does not make provisions?
It's valuable to keep one's name intact.
The great path is broad and open,
small trails compete to lead ahead.
Mysterious yellow is dusty and defiled,
while red and purple shine bright.
Alas for Kǒng-fù, my master,
whose sagely virtue comprehended profundity.
Such honors not grounded in righteousness,
suddenly vanish like dust and smoke.
Although I lack spiritual virtue,
I wish to hide in profound depths.
Morning clouds gather from all sides,
dispersed at dawn and dusk.
Pure light casts its rays,
the morning star still shines bright.
Solemnly soars the luán,
harmoniously cries the wild geese.
Now I find no joy,
and the years and months slip by.
Old Jiāng supported Zhōu,
and Zǐfáng aided Hàn.
Responding to fate, they assisted the Mandate,
their achievements quieted chaos.
With their persons, their merits became renowned,
and through virtue, their names praised.
The world lacks such deeds today,
and talents do not fit the times.
Entrust destiny to what is given,
and accept Heaven without resentment.
Alas, gentlemen such as you,
why do you sigh so long?
The sun and moon shine abundantly,
able to illuminate Heaven’s wisdom.
Three august ones preside over the court,
three groups of eight rise to office.
They raise the outstanding and talented,
and dismiss the stubborn and evil.
The highest sets up virtue,
next is the establishment of achievement.
The wind of benevolence spreads broadly,
and the subtle transformation penetrates deeply.
Fortunate to encounter this flourishing brightness,
I witness the harmony of the age.
Lingering quietly by the lowly gate,
I follow only where my resolve leads.
Going out and staying in are different paths,
lowering and raising my head show different expressions.
I gaze and sigh for ancient heroes,
aspiring to those lofty tracks.
I admire Mount Jīshān,
and suddenly think of Yú Lóng.
Climbing high, I gaze far,
and look all around the eight points.
Mountains and rivers stretch distant and remote,
the long road winds and diverges.
I am affected by Mòzǐ,
and cherish Yáng Zhū.
Embracing my shadow, I stand like a swan,
raising my head but hesitating and lingering.
Looking up, I gaze at soaring birds,
looking down, I see swimming fish.
Vermilion woods shrouded in cloud,
green leaves loosened by the wind.
Creation is mysterious and harmonious,
myriads of things flourish in profusion.
When great, it is never sufficient;
when restrained, there is surplus.
Why sustain my resolve,
but to keep to simplicity and emptiness?
Yet I wish for a different age,
for ten thousand years to share in harmony.
Faint and humble are my followers,
orderly and attuned to great principles.
Diligently studying the ancient texts,
thoughts linger and delay.
Thus I order my servant,
raising words to set out on a journey.
Vast and mighty is the river,
gently floating is the willow boat.
Looking up, I gaze at the shining radiance,
looking down, I watch the flowing waves.
The sun and moon move eastward,
their light fading in the west.
Cold departs and heat returns,
the four seasons replace each other in turn.
Blossoms flourish in luxuriant spring,
dense leaves fall in withered autumn.
Prime years wane into decline,
suddenly like a floating dream,
Carefree and at ease,
without blame in this world.
I journey to the northern woods,
wandering along the river’s shore.
Looking up, I cling to jade trunks,
looking down, I see pale threads.
The hidden phoenix folds its wings,
the hidden dragon leaps with its scales.
Subtle light conceals its glow,
and forms transform in accord with spirit.
The gentleman advances in virtue,
in hardship keeping his thoughts pure.
To amass wealth brings reproach,
but a bamboo bowl and gourd are called benevolence.
Yí Shū gathered wild herbs,
pure and lofty, his repute extended far.
Lord Jǐng of Qí had a thousand chariots,
yet it was all but dust and dirt.
Alas, you later generations,
thrive as these among humankind.
A humble thatched gate, a square hole for light,
and this is called the true Way.
The dazzling beauty of Huáróng,
is outstanding among her generation.
Enchanting and extraordinarily lovely,
graceful as if pure and elegant.
With dark hair and arched brows,
her radiance stretches far and wide.
Her style is ornate and luxurious,
her fragrance follows the wind.
Turning back, one perceives her essence,
her spirit soars and flies.
The noble man disciplines himself,
his heart pure as ice and frost.
Confusion and darkness abound,
as in days past with the Two Wángs.
Jade terraces and spinning chambers,
through endless night, golden beams.
The house of Yīn failed the Xià,
Zhōu overthrew Zhòu of Shāng.
Alas for their descendants,
one can only grieve.
The morning breeze sweeps the dust,
the dawn rain sprinkles the road.
Swift chariots fly like dragons,
sorrowful cries looking outward.
Grasping the reins and pressing the whip,
advancing and retreating with measure.
Joy goes, sorrow comes,
pensive, the heart understands.
Thinking of the courteous person,
endlessly caring, turning back.
The sun and moon revolve and depart,
the year swiftly nears its dusk.
Alas, I am young,
yet dull and stubborn.
How could I not aspire far?
Yet talent is hard to admire and pursue.
Life is not like gold or stone,
the body light as morning dew.
How to know the longevity of Sōng and Qiáo?
Nourishing the spirit, most primordial.
Freely wandering beyond the realm,
my years rise in fortune.
Poem:
Heaven and earth are enveloped in mist,
prime essence changes with the ages.
Pure brightness illuminates spirits,
harmonious airs flow gently.
In shining imperial court,
Yī Héng became an assistant.
My talent is not truly literary,
nor is my capacity for martial accomplishments;
I went to Yuán and Xiāng,
entrusting myself to the companion fisherman,
leisurely!
At ease!
Dwelling here, abiding here.
The moon is bright and stars are sparse,
the sky high and air cold.
Whistling and singing, I grieve in my heart,
alone I awake and speak in my dreams.
Facing the cup, clutching my breast,
at meals I forget to eat.
There is no day-lily in this world
to ease my sorrow and sighs!
